task.description:
You are on branch feature/WF03-ISS0881-20260929 (checkout it if not already). Read handoffs/WF03-ISS0881-20260929/step-01-issue-fixer-diagnose.json's result.summary in full -- it is ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis of ISS-0881, which you are designing a fix for. Root cause (as diagnosed): `sandbox_schema_names/0` (test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs:571-582) does an UNSCOPED, platform-wide read of every `sandbox_%` schema in `information_schema.schemata`, with no filter tying it to this test's own pool instance. Under scripts/test_parallel.sh's full-contention run, at least 8 other test files in the suite legitimately create/drop real `sandbox_%` schemas via their own SandboxPool usage concurrently in other OS-process partitions -- any one of them creating or dropping a schema during RT-6's baseline-to-final window can flip `assert final == baseline` (line 1127) and/or (if it happens to touch a name already tracked) `refute MapSet.member?(final, o_schema)` (line 1126), even though RT-6's OWN pool behaved correctly throughout. This is a test-isolation defect in the test file only -- no production code path in lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex is implicated.

Design a fix (design artefact only -- no implementation code) that reframes RT-6's (and any other test in this file using the same before/after `sandbox_schema_names()` pattern -- grep the file for every call site of `sandbox_schema_names/0` and `drop_sandbox_schemas_created_since!/1` before scoping your design, since a fix to the helper itself needs to keep every existing call site correct) before/after schema-leak check so it is immune to a concurrent, unrelated partition creating/dropping its OWN sandbox schema during the test's baseline-to-final window, while still catching a REAL leak from the pool under test. Concretely, your design must specify:
1. The exact new comparison RT-6 (and any other affected test) should assert instead of `final == baseline` -- e.g. asserting only that no NEW member of the (final - baseline) set collides with a name this test's OWN pool ever minted, or an equivalent formulation that stops depending on the full platform-wide set being quiescent.
2. Whether `sandbox_schema_names/0` itself needs a signature/behavior change (e.g. an optional exclusion or scoping parameter) or whether the fix is purely in how each test call site COMPARES what it already gets back -- state which and why.
3. The exact function signatures/@spec-style shapes for anything you add or change (design docs never contain full Elixir implementation bodies -- signatures and shapes only, per your own role's constraint).
4. Confirmation this design does not weaken the test's actual regression-catching power for a REAL schema leak from RT-6's own pool (the whole point of the original assertion) -- name explicitly what invariant the new assertion still proves.

Write the design artefact to lib/letflow/design/iss0881-sandbox-pool-test-isolation.md, following this project's existing design-doc conventions (see other files already in lib/letflow/design/ for the expected shape/sections if you need a reference). Commit it to the feature branch and complete this handoff (status COMPLETED, result.status PASS/FAIL/PARTIAL per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md, next_action pointing to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR). Do not modify the task block. Run `mix letflow.lint_handoffs --dir handoffs/WF03-ISS0881-20260929` before finishing and fix any WARN.
acceptance_criteria: Design artefact at lib/letflow/design/iss0881-sandbox-pool-test-isolation.md, no implementation code bodies (signatures/shapes only)
Every existing call site of sandbox_schema_names/0 and drop_sandbox_schemas_created_since!/1 in test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs identified and addressed (not just RT-6)
The new comparison is concretely specified, not left as 'make it more robust'
Design explicitly states what real-leak-detection guarantee is preserved
No production code (lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex) touched unless the design explicitly justifies why the test-only fix is insufficient
